A stack-based buffer overflow vulnerability exists in the web management interface of affected Moxa wireless device servers. An authenticated remote attacker with low privileges could exploit insufficient bounds checking of user-supplied input, causing the web management service to become unresponsive. Restoring the service requires power cycling the affected device, while other device functions remain operational.

In affected versions of Octopus Server, OIDC token issuer validation was performed inconsistently. This could result in a token issued from a suitably configured non legitimate issuer being accepted as a token belonging to a service account from a legitimate trusted issuer. Exploitation requires a service account with at least one OIDC identity configured. An attacker would also need to know or guess some details of that identity in order to be in a position to attempt exploitation.

Semantic MediaWiki 3.0.0 before 7.3.1 contains an uncontrolled recursion vulnerability in LegacyParser::getSubqueryDescription() that processes nested query tokens before depth limits apply. Unauthenticated attackers can submit deeply nested query elements to the action=ask API to consume substantial CPU and memory, tying up request workers.

SemanticMediaWiki from 3.0.0 before 7.3.1 contains a reflected cross-site scripting vulnerability in Special:Ask, which outputs separator parameters (sep, propsep, valuesep, delim, separator) without HTML escaping in list, category, DSV, and CSV result printers. Unauthenticated attackers can send victims crafted Special:Ask links using request_type=raw or request_type=special_page to execute JavaScript in the wiki's origin, stealing sessions or CSRF tokens.

Semantic MediaWiki from 2.5.0 before 7.3.1 contains an uncontrolled resource consumption vulnerability that allows anonymous attackers to force quadratic computation by supplying a zero limit to Special:PropertyLabelSimilarity. Attackers can send repeated requests with limit=0 to bypass the SQL LIMIT and trigger pairwise similar_text() comparisons, exhausting PHP CPU, memory, and database connections.

Semantic MediaWiki from 7.3.0 before 7.3.1 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in the smwtask update task that allows users with edit rights to force semantic updates on arbitrary pages. Attackers can supply a serialized subject parameter for a restricted page to trigger forced reparsing, semantic-store writes, and resource-intensive dependency work.

Semantic MediaWiki from 3.0.0 before 7.3.1 contains a cross-site request forgery vulnerability in Special:SMWAdmin because it overwrites the wpEditToken with a freshly generated valid token. Attackers can lure an authenticated smw-admin user to a malicious page that triggers schema setup, entity-disposal, or job actions, causing semantic data loss and resource exhaustion.

Semantic MediaWiki from 3.0.0 before 7.3.1 contains a cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows attackers to inject markup by storing malicious semantic property values rendered unescaped in autocomplete suggestions. When another user opens the property-value autocomplete with an empty query, jquery.autocomplete.js concatenates the raw PValueLookup API value into HTML via container.html(), altering the dropdown and potentially executing script.

Semantic MediaWiki from 4.2.0 before 7.3.1 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows authenticated profile or schema editors to inject HTML through FacetedSearch exploration-link labels. Attackers can store markup in the label, which ExploreListBuilder::buildHTML() passes unescaped to Html::rawElement(), altering the Special:FacetedSearch page and potentially running scripts in viewers' browsers.

Semantic MediaWiki from 3.1.0 before 7.3.1 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows authenticated schema editors to inject HTML through schema descriptions. Attackers with the smw-schemaedit permission can save HTML that is passed unescaped to Html::rawElement() in HtmlBuilder, altering pages and targeting users who view the schema.

Semantic MediaWiki from 3.1.0 before 7.3.1 contains a reflected cross-site scripting vulnerability in the Special:SMWAdmin ID lookup that allows unauthenticated attackers to inject markup through the unescaped id parameter. Attackers can lure an smw-admin administrator into opening a crafted lookup link, bypassing the auto-satisfied edit-token check, to execute script and perform privileged actions in the administrator's session.

Semantic MediaWiki from 3.0.0 before 7.3.1 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows users with page-edit rights to inject HTML through Keyword-typed property values rendered unescaped on Special:Browse. Attackers can annotate a Keyword property with an event-handler payload that executes JavaScript in viewers' sessions, including administrators, to read tokens and perform actions.

SemanticMediaWiki from 4.2.0 before 7.2.1 contains a reflected cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to inject HTML via unescaped cstate parameters in Special:FacetedSearch. Attackers can craft URLs with q, a matching crc32 csum or filtered=1, and cstate values that break out of hidden input attributes to execute script in victims' browsers.

REDAXO before 5.21.5 contains a cross-site request forgery vulnerability because the backend processes the safemode GET parameter in index.php without validating a CSRF token. Attackers can lure a logged-in administrator into opening a crafted link to disable global safe mode, writing safe_mode: false to config.yml, or enable session safe mode, disabling backend addons.

REDAXO before 5.21.4 contains a broken access control vulnerability that allows authenticated editors to modify slices in unauthorized categories by pairing a permitted article with a foreign slice id. Attackers can abuse content/edit delete and edit functions or the content_slice_status and content_move_slice APIs to delete, toggle, move, or overwrite other editors' slices.

In affected versions of Octopus Server, creating a user invitation writes the invitation code to the audit event log. When the invitation is linked to a space, a user in that space with appropriate permissions could read the code from the audit event. Successfully exploiting this by redeeming the unclaimed invitation could allow the user to escalate privileges however this is dependant on the permissions assigned for the invited user.
In affected versions of Octopus Server, a user holding the System Manager role could escalate their privileges to full system Administrator.
In JetBrains Junie CLI before 26.8.17 command execution was possible due to incomplete validation of allowlisted commands

REDAXO before 5.21.3 contains a cross-site request forgery vulnerability in the structure/history plugin that allows attackers to delete history or roll back content via unvalidated GET requests. Attackers can lure logged-in backend users to a page triggering func=clearall or rex_history_function=snap, permanently deleting all article snapshots or reverting articles to earlier states.

REDAXO before 5.21.0 contains a reflected cross-site scripting vulnerability in the backend packages API, where the function parameter is concatenated into an error message rendered without HTML escaping. Attackers can lure an authenticated backend user to a crafted link containing a valid CSRF token, executing JavaScript that performs same-origin actions or reads DOM data.

Joomla Extension - dj-extensions.com - Unauthenticated Stored XSS in DJ-HelpfulArticles < 1.3.0 - The “was this article helpful” voting widget posts a client-supplied ip field to its AJAX handlers (getDeny, getConfirm, getDenyReason in mod_djhelpful_articles/helper.php), reachable without authentication through com_ajax. The value was stored exactly as submitted instead of being taken from the connection by the server. It was then printed without output escaping in the administrator backend’s “Helpful articles” overview (views/items/tmpl/default.php). $db->quote() was applied on insert, which protects the SQL statement but does nothing for HTML output. There was no CSRF token, no rate limit, and the vote de-duplication keyed on the same attacker-controlled field.

@fastify/express is a Fastify plugin that runs Express middleware inside Fastify. In versions 4.0.5 through 4.0.8, when Fastify runs with the non-default ignoreDuplicateSlashes option enabled, the plugin matches path-scoped Express middleware against a URL whose duplicate-slash normalization has also collapsed the separator after an absolute-form request target's scheme, so Fastify's router resolves the request to the scoped path and runs the handler while the Express layer no longer sees that path. As a result, a request using an absolute-form target can reach a handler on a scoped route such as an admin path while the middleware for authentication, authorization, or rate limiting is skipped. An unauthenticated attacker needs only the non-default ignoreDuplicateSlashes option to be enabled. The issue is fixed in @fastify/express 4.0.9, and users should upgrade to 4.0.9 or later. As a workaround, enforce authentication in a Fastify hook such as preHandler that runs after the router resolves the request, or leave ignoreDuplicateSlashes at its default.

In Eclipse ioFog iofogctl versions 1.0.0 through 3.7.0 and 3.8.0-rc.1 through 3.9.1, the provisioning key and CA certificate returned by the Controller API are concatenated into shell commands (`edgelet provision` and `edgelet config cert` on supported releases; `iofog-agent provision` and `iofog-agent cert` on older releases) that run over SSH on a remote agent host and via a local shell. A party who can change that API response can include shell metacharacters and cause the operator's CLI to run additional commands on the agent host when the operator deploys or attaches an agent. This is fixed in version 3.9.2.

In Eclipse ioFog Operator versions 3.8.0 before 3.9.2, TLS certificate verification is disabled when the operator contacts the Controller API and when it logs in to an external OIDC issuer. An on-path attacker can present any certificate, capture the OAuth client secret (external mode) or the Controller bootstrap admin password (embedded mode with Controller HTTPS enabled), and supply the access token the operator stores for later Controller API calls. v3.8 removed Keycloak. The exposed credential is not a Keycloak realm-admin secret.

In `github.com/eclipse-keypont/crypto11/v2` versions `>= 2.0.0-rc3, <= 2.0.0-rc8`, the ML-KEM key-pair lookup functions (`FindMLKEMKeyPair`, `FindMLKEMKeyPairs`, `FindMLKEMKeyPairsWithAttributes`) locate the public half of an ML-KEM key pair by `CKA_ID`/`CKA_LABEL` and never verify it against the private key. In addition, the "ID only" fallback search runs even when the private key has no `CKA_ID`, so the search template reduces to the public-key class and the ML-KEM key type and the first ML-KEM public key on the token is returned. `Encapsulate()` on the resulting key pair encrypts the fresh shared secret to that key, so its owner — not the holder of the private key the caller looked up — can recover the secret. An attacker who can open an unauthenticated session on the token and plant a public `CKK_ML_KEM` object carrying the victim's `CKA_ID`/`CKA_LABEL` receives the shared secrets for encapsulations performed through the substituted key pair, compromising the confidentiality of those secrets and of everything protected by keys derived from them. The v1 module paths have no ML-KEM support and are not affected.

@fastify/session is a session plugin for Fastify. In all releases before 11.1.6, with the default rolling session behavior, a request that restored a session before a logout could save its own copy after another request had completed the session destroy call, recreating the destroyed session identifier with its authenticated data. An attacker who already holds a victim's valid signed session cookie and keeps a request in flight across the logout can replay that cookie to restore the session after it was meant to be revoked, without any cookie theft or signature forgery. The issue is fixed in @fastify/session 11.1.6, which adds a per session generation marker and a conditional store write so a session restored before a logout or regeneration cannot recreate or overwrite the current entry, and users should upgrade to 11.1.6 or later. There is no workaround, and custom session stores must implement the new conditional write.

An OS command vulnerability exists in CoreTec product that allows authenticated users with certain roles to execute arbitrary system commands with full control over the device. The vulnerability exists in the configuration daemon's time synchronization handler, which is responsible for setting the system time-zone. When processing time-zone configuration updates, the daemon constructs a shell command by concatenating user-supplied input without any sanitization or validation.

Eaton easyE4 uses a static nonce during authentication, which could allow an unauthenticated attacker with access to captured authentication traffic to replay a valid authentication exchange and gain unauthorized access to the device.

Eaton easyE4 uses an insufficiently strong password policy. An attacker who obtains a password hash, including through CVE-2026-41020, could perform an offline password-guessing attack and potentially recover user credentials.

Eaton easySoft improperly validates TLS certificates presented by easyE4 devices. A network-adjacent attacker could exploit this weakness to perform a man-in-the-middle attack and potentially intercept or modify communications between easySoft and easyE4.

Unrestricted Upload of File with Dangerous Type vulnerability in the PuMuKIT application allows a unauthenticated user to upload any type of file to the server, and to any path where the web server user has write permissions. This could also allow them to delete files.

Docker Desktop before version 4.97.0 could write third-party API keys and OAuth access tokens in cleartext to local application logs and diagnostics bundles due to insufficient IPC payload redaction. An attacker with read access to these files could obtain the credentials. These OAuth tokens are not Docker account tokens. Docker Desktop 4.94.0 and 4.95.0 addressed the known logging paths, but logs containing credentials can remain after upgrading. Docker Desktop 4.97.0 fixes the issue and includes cleanup of existing host logs and crash dumps.

An attacker can read the name of filesystem paths of your application present via Tidewave configuration via /tidewave/connect or via the rendered toolbar.

Neither response checks the Host header. A web page that rebinds its own domain to the loopback address can therefore read the tag with a same-origin request, which carries no Origin header. The paths usually reveal the local username and the project layout.

This issue affects tidewave: from 0.8.0 before 0.9.2.

The Tables app's share-listing endpoint (GET /apps/tables/share/table/{tableId}) did not verify that the requesting user has manage-level permission on the table before returning the full list of share recipients (users, groups, and teams) along with their permission levels. A user who was only granted read-data access to a table, and who is correctly prevented from seeing this information in the web UI, could call the endpoint directly to enumerate everyone the table is shared with and their access levels.

This does not expose the table's data itself beyond what the read-data grant already permits, only the list of share recipients and their permission levels.

This does not grant access to the contents of the discovered resources themselves, only their existence, names, and identifiers.

GnuPG (version 2.5.21) for Windows contains a vulnerability where default Discretionary Access Control List (DACL) inheritance on the C:\ProgramData directory allows members of the BUILTIN\Users group to create arbitrary subdirectories under this path. NextChat version 2.16.1 contains a client‑side cross‑site scripting (XSS) vulnerability in the Plugin Editor due to unsafe rendering of externally supplied OpenAPI plugin schema content. When a plugin schema is loaded from a remote URL, the returned content is stored in plugin.content and later rendered using React’s dangerouslySetInnerHTML without proper sanitization. An attacker can host a malicious OpenAPI schema containing HTML or JavaScript markup and trick a user into loading it through the Plugin Editor, resulting in arbitrary JavaScript execution in the NextChat origin. Successful exploitation allows access to JavaScript‑readable cookies and other client‑side data associated with the NextChat application.

descriptions.value: MISP Guard, a proxy that enforces security policies on MISP feed data, contained an incomplete validation check for required taxonomy tags. When a feed event or its attributes carried tags belonging to a required taxonomy (for example, TLP), the guard only verified that at least one tag of that taxonomy matched the configured allowed list. It did not verify that every tag of the required taxonomy present on the event or attribute was in the allowed list. As a result, an event or attribute could simultaneously carry an allowed tag (e.g., tlp:clear) and a non-allowed tag (e.g., tlp:red or tlp:amber) and still pass the guard's policy check. This allowed data marked with a higher classification or sensitivity level to be distributed through feeds configured to only distribute lower-classification data, effectively bypassing the intended data-handling restrictions. The vulnerability affected both event-level and attribute-level tag validation, including attributes nested within objects and shadow attributes. An attacker with the ability to author or modify MISP events in a feed source could include non-allowed taxonomy tags alongside allowed ones to exfiltrate more sensitive data to feed consumers than the guard policy intended to permit.

When a message containing an OpenPGP key attachment was displayed, Thunderbird automatically loaded the attachment's content to offer importing the key. A sender could mark the attachment as an external attachment pointing to an arbitrary URL, which Thunderbird then loaded without any user interaction, bypassing remote content blocking. On Windows, a URL pointing to an attacker-controlled network share could leak the user's NTLM credentials.
The NTLM credential leak only affects Thunderbird on Windows. On other operating systems, the issue allowed a remote request that bypassed remote content blocking. This vulnerability was fixed in Thunderbird 159 and Thunderbird 153.6.

When replying to, forwarding, or editing a crafted email message as new, Thunderbird could embed parts of a different message stored in the same folder into the message being composed, without showing a blocked content warning. If the user sent the message, the content of the other message was disclosed to the recipients. This vulnerability was fixed in Thunderbird 159 and Thunderbird 153.6.

Thunderbird's check that prevents mailbox: URLs from accessing files on remote Windows network shares could be bypassed using extended-length UNC paths. Displaying a specially crafted email could cause Thunderbird to connect to an SMB server chosen by the attacker, disclosing the user's Windows account name and NTLM authentication data, which could be used for offline password cracking or relay attacks.
This bug only affects Thunderbird on Windows. Other operating systems are unaffected. This vulnerability was fixed in Thunderbird 159 and Thunderbird 153.6.

When looking for calendars in a directory on a server, during account setup or when adding a new network calendar, Thunderbird accepted calendar locations pointing to other servers, local files or network shares. A malicious server, or a network attacker when the lookup used plain HTTP, could make Thunderbird subscribe to such a location. On Windows this could leak the user's NTLM credentials to an attacker-controlled host on every calendar refresh, and changes to the calendar could be written to the attacker's share or overwrite a local file. This vulnerability was fixed in Thunderbird 159 and Thunderbird 153.6.

A remote RSS feed could use the itunes:new-feed-url or newLocation element to permanently change its stored subscription URL to a file: URL. Thunderbird then read that location on every feed update. This allowed a malicious feed, or an attacker able to modify a feed delivered over HTTP, to make Thunderbird read local files and, on Windows, connect to an attacker-controlled network share, which could leak the user's NTLM credentials.
The NTLM credential leak only affects Thunderbird on Windows. Other operating systems are affected by the local file read only. This vulnerability was fixed in Thunderbird 159 and Thunderbird 153.6.

Clicking a news: or snews: link that referenced a message-ID made Thunderbird connect, without asking, to the host and port given in the link, even if it was not a configured news server. Line breaks in the message-ID were sent to the server unmodified, so a crafted link could send arbitrary commands to services reachable from the user's network. In addition, snews: links to such servers connected without TLS. This vulnerability was fixed in Thunderbird 159 and Thunderbird 153.6.

When logging in to a Matrix account, Thunderbird used the homeserver address provided in the server's login response without validating it. A malicious or compromised homeserver could provide a file: URL, causing Thunderbird to send all further Matrix requests of that session to local files or, on Windows, to an attacker-controlled network share, which could leak the user's NTLM credentials.
The NTLM credential leak only affects Thunderbird on Windows. Other operating systems are unaffected. This vulnerability was fixed in Thunderbird 159 and Thunderbird 153.6.
Response body and chunk parsing would handle non-hex or negative integers incorrectly which could result in misinterpreting HTTP response contents.

The MembershipWorks plugin for WordPress before 6.17 contains an information disclosure vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to access member-only content through the WordPress REST API. Because the filter that strips protected content for non-members is only attached during normal front-end request handling and not during REST API requests, an unauthenticated attacker can retrieve the raw member-only content in a post or page’s rendered content, bypassing the plugin’s content protection.

When coalescing adjacent text nodes in addText and fosterParent, appending to an existing TextNode's Data via string concatenation (n.Data += text) reallocated and copied the accumulated string on every token. Inputs containing many short text runs separated by ignored end tags (such as "a</x>") caused O(n^2) allocations and byte copies. Accumulate coalesced text in per-node byte slices during parsing and materialize Data strings once at the end of parse.

In childTextNodesAreLiteral, walking up the tree previously stopped at the nearest foreign ancestor once an HTML integration point was found. However, that integration point may itself be a descendant of an element that was foster-parented into a foreign namespace (such as <mglyph> or <malignmark> fostered under <mtext>), causing a parser to resolve the subtree in a different foreign namespace upon re-parsing the rendered output. Continue walking the full ancestor chain and verify that every transition from a non-empty namespace occurs at an HTML integration point before emitting literal text.

The private keys of eight eMudhra intermediate CA certificates have been compromised. eMudhra revoked the eight affected intermediate certificates on October 18, 2026. ProtobufParser parses length-prefixed protobuf string and bytes fields by checking (_inputPtr + len) <= _inputEnd and then, on the fast path, calling _finishShortText(len). Both use 32-bit signed integer arithmetic. When an attacker supplies a varint decoding to a length near Integer.MAX_VALUE, _inputPtr + len overflows to a negative value, the bounds check passes, and _finishShortText(len) reaches TextBuffer.expandCurrentSegment(len), which performs Arrays.copyOf with no cap and throws OutOfMemoryError: Requested array size exceeds VM limit.



The JVM refuses arrays larger than Integer.MAX_VALUE - 8 before consulting available heap, so -Xmx tuning does not mitigate the issue. StreamReadConstraints.maxStringLength and maxDocumentLength do not gate this path: a 33-byte payload is far below any document-length cap and the string-length check does not fire before the allocation. This was confirmed empirically against shipping artifacts with maxStringLength, maxDocumentLength and maxNestingDepth all configured.



A February 2026 hardening commit added the equivalent overflow guard to the packed-array-length and message-length paths but left the string-length call sites unguarded. No privileges or user interaction beyond the ability to submit data for parsing are required.

The asynchronous Smile parser (NonBlockingByteArrayParser) uses a raw-binary length prefix taken from untrusted input to allocate a byte[] before the body is read, with no upper bound and no overflow check. On the raw-binary marker 0xFD, _decodeVInt() computes (value << 6) + (i & 0x3F) without the (value >>> 25) != 0 overflow guard present in the blocking SmileParser._readUnsignedVInt, and _startRawBinary then allocates the declared length immediately.



A Smile feed of roughly ten bytes can therefore force an eager allocation of approximately 2 GB, producing an OutOfMemoryError on reactive or asynchronous Smile endpoints. A VInt crafted to overflow int yields a negative length and a NegativeArraySizeException, a RuntimeException that is not a JacksonException and so escapes the parser contract. Either outcome crashes the request or processing thread.



This is the same class of issue as CVE-2020-28491 in the CBOR parser of this library, which was fixed with a LONGEST_NON_CHUNKED_BINARY guard; the asynchronous Smile parser never received the equivalent guard. No privileges or user interaction beyond the ability to submit data for parsing are required.

GROWI contains an authorization bypass vulnerability in its page viewing and commenting functionality due to improper use of a user-controlled key. By exploiting this vulnerability, an authenticated attacker may obtain the contents and comments of pages without the required read permission.

GROWI contains an authorization bypass vulnerability in its tag update API and the page update API due to improper use of a user-controlled key. By exploiting this vulnerability, an attacker who can log in to the product may obtain the contents of pages without the required read permission and save them to pages that the attacker can edit.

GROWI contains a missing authorization check vulnerability in its collaborative editing feature. By exploiting this vulnerability, a user with read-only permission, including a guest user, or a user in pending, suspended, or invited status may modify page drafts.

NexoPOS through 6.3.0 contains a missing authorization vulnerability that allows authenticated cashiers to manipulate other cashiers' register sessions because CashRegistersService never compares used_by with the user. Attackers holding the default nexopos.use.registers permission can submit closing, cash-in, or cash-out actions to POST /api/cash-registers/{action}/{register} to force-close sessions or alter balances.

mews/pos through 2.0.0 contains an insufficient verification of data authenticity vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to forge payment results by submitting unverified callbacks. GarantiPos, PayForPos and InterPos 3D Pay and 3D Host handlers skip check3DHash(), letting attackers post tampered status, amount or order ID fields to complete orders without paying.

The Enable Media Replace plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to authorization bypass in all versions up to, and including, 4.2.2. This is due to the plugin not properly verifying that a user is authorized to perform an action. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with author-level access and above, to modify the post_content of any published post referencing the replaced media — including Administrator-owned posts — making changes immediately visible to unauthenticated visitors. The doReplaceQuery() method performs a database-wide search-and-replace across all posts containing the old media URL without any per-post capability check, meaning a single Author-triggered request can silently overwrite a large number of posts that WordPress's standard admin UI and REST API would otherwise forbid that user from editing.

El plugin Enable Media Replace para WordPress es vulnerable a una omisión de autorización en todas las versiones hasta la 4.2.2 incluida. Esto se debe a que el plugin no verifica correctamente que un usuario está autorizado para realizar una acción. Esto permite a atacantes autenticados, con acceso de nivel de autor y superior, modificar el post_content de cualquier entrada publicada que haga referencia al medio reemplazado - incluyendo entradas propiedad de Administradores - haciendo que los cambios sean inmediatamente visibles para visitantes no autenticados. El método doReplaceQuery() realiza una búsqueda y reemplazo en toda la base de datos en todas las entradas que contienen la URL del medio antiguo sin ninguna verificación de capacidad por entrada, lo que significa que una única solicitud iniciada por un Autor puede sobrescribir silenciosamente un gran número de entradas que la interfaz de usuario de administración estándar de WordPress y la API REST de otro modo prohibirían a ese usuario editar.

The MemberPress plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Cross-Site Request Forgery in versions up to, and including, 1.14.1. This is due to a bypassable nonce verification check in the save_profile_fields() function that uses an isset() condition at line 1119, allowing the security check to be completely bypassed by simply omitting the nonce parameter from the request. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to change authenticated users' email addresses via a forged request granted they can trick an authenticated user into performing an action such as clicking on a link, leading to account takeover through password reset functionality.

El plugin MemberPress para WordPress es vulnerable a falsificación de petición en sitios cruzados (CSRF) en versiones hasta la 1.14.1 incluida. Esto se debe a una verificación de nonce eludible en la función save_profile_fields() que utiliza una condición isset() en la línea 1119, lo que permite que la verificación de seguridad sea completamente eludida simplemente omitiendo el parámetro nonce de la petición. Esto hace posible que atacantes no autenticados cambien las direcciones de correo electrónico de usuarios autenticados mediante una petición falsificada, siempre que puedan engañar a un usuario autenticado para que realice una acción como hacer clic en un enlace, lo que lleva a la toma de control de la cuenta a través de la funcionalidad de restablecimiento de contraseña.

Dell PowerProtect Data Domain, Feature Release versions 7.7.1.0 through 8.8, LTS2024 release versions 7.13.1.0 through 7.13.1.80, LTS2025 release versions 8.3.1.0 through 8.3.1.40, LTS2026 release versions 8.6.1.0 through 8.6.1.20, contain an Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal') vulnerability. An unauthenticated attacker with remote access could potentially exploit this vulnerability, leading to Filesystem access for attacker.

Local privilege escalation due to improper authentication. The following products are affected: Acronis Cyber Protect Cloud Agent (Windows) before build 42569, Acronis Cyber Protect 17 (Windows) before build 42587.

Escalada de privilegios local debido a una autenticación incorrecta. Los siguientes productos se ven afectados: Acronis Cyber Protect Cloud Agent (Windows) antes de la compilación 42569, Acronis Cyber Protect 17 (Windows) antes de la compilación 42587.

Dell PowerProtect Data Domain Management Center, Feature Release versions 7.7.1.0 through 8.8, LTS2024 release versions 7.13.1.0 through 7.13.1.80, LTS2025 release versions 8.3.1.0 through 8.3.1.40, LTS2026 release versions 8.6.1.0 through 8.6.1.20, contain a Missing Authorization vulnerability. A low privileged attacker with remote access could potentially exploit this vulnerability, leading to Unauthorized operation.

Xibo is an open source digital signage platform with a web content management system and Windows display player software. Prior to 4.4.3, missing access-control checks on `GET /dataset/export/csv/{id}` allow an authenticated user to export data from any dataset, including datasets created by administrators, by iterating over `sequential dataset IDs`. Exploitation requires access to the privilege allowing edits, including deletion, to all created `DataSets` independently of Layouts. This privilege is not granted to non-administrators as standard. This issue is fixed in version 4.4.3.

Xibo es una plataforma de señalización digital de código abierto con un sistema de gestión de contenido web y software de reproductor de pantalla para Windows. Versiones anteriores a la 4.4.3, la falta de comprobaciones de control de acceso en “GET /dataset/export/csv/{id}” permite a un usuario autenticado exportar datos de cualquier conjunto de datos, incluidos los conjuntos de datos creados por administradores, al iterar sobre los ID de conjuntos de datos secuenciales. La explotación requiere acceso al privilegio que permite ediciones, incluida la eliminación, de todos los “DataSets” creados independientemente de los “Layouts”. Este privilegio no se concede a los no administradores de forma predeterminada. Este problema se solucionó en la versión 4.4.3.

Xibo is an open source digital signage platform with a web content management system and Windows display player software. Prior to 4.4.3, missing access-control checks on `PUT/DELETE /action/{id}` allow an authenticated user to modify or delete actions on any Layout. Exploitation requires the privilege to allow edits, including deletion, to all created Layouts, which is granted to non-administrators as standard. This issue concerns `Layout actions` rather than the separately reported DataSet export vulnerability. This issue is fixed in version 4.4.3.

Xibo es una plataforma de señalización digital de código abierto con un sistema de gestión de contenido web y software de reproductor de pantalla para Windows. Versiones anteriores a la 4.4.3, la falta de comprobaciones de control de acceso en “PUT/DELETE /action/{id}” permite a un usuario autenticado modificar o eliminar acciones en cualquier Diseño (Layout). La explotación requiere el privilegio de permitir ediciones, incluida la eliminación, en todos los Diseños (Layouts) creados, lo cual se concede a los usuarios no administradores de forma estándar. Este problema se refiere a las ’acciones de Diseño (Layout)’ en lugar de la vulnerabilidad de exportación de DataSet reportada por separado. Este problema está corregido en la versión 4.4.3.

NORA is a self-hosted artifact registry and pull-through cache. Prior to 0.9.5, `nora-registry` authenticates the token-management UI but fails to require administrator authorization. `auth_middleware()` protects `/ui/tokens` and `/api/ui/tokens`, but state-changing requests are checked only with `role.can_write()`, not `role.can_admin()`. `tokens_page()` and `tokens_list()` call `store.list_all_tokens()`, exposing IDs and metadata across all users, while `tokens_revoke()` calls `store.revoke_token` using the supplied token ID without an ownership or admin check. A read bearer token can enumerate other users' token existence, owner, role, description, expiry and last-use metadata. A write bearer token or write-capable OIDC identity can additionally revoke arbitrary admin and service tokens, disrupting the registry and forcing credential recovery. Read-only identities cannot POST a revocation. This issue is fixed in version 0.9.5.

NORA es un registro de artefactos autoalojado y una caché de paso. Versiones anteriores a la 0.9.5, “nora-registry” autentica la interfaz de usuario de gestión de tokens, pero no exige la autorización de administrador. “auth_middleware()” protege “/ui/tokens” y “/api/ui/tokens”, pero las solicitudes que cambian el estado se verifican solo con “role.can_write()”, no con “role.can_admin()”. “tokens_page()” y “tokens_list()” llaman a “store.list_all_tokens()”, exponiendo IDs y metadatos de todos los usuarios, mientras que “tokens_revoke()” llama a “store.revoke_token” utilizando el ID de token proporcionado sin una verificación de propiedad o de administrador. Un token portador de lectura puede enumerar la existencia, el propietario, el rol, la descripción, la caducidad y los metadatos de último uso de los tokens de otros usuarios. Un token portador de escritura o una identidad OIDC con capacidad de escritura puede, además, revocar tokens de administrador y de servicio arbitrarios, interrumpiendo el registro y forzando la recuperación de credenciales. Las identidades de solo lectura no pueden realizar una solicitud POST de revocación. Este problema se solucionó en la versión 0.9.5.

OpenHop is a tool for creating interactive data-flow diagrams. Prior to 0.3.7, `@openhop/server` passes unauthenticated flow route parameters from `GET /api/flows/:id` and `DELETE /api/flows/:id` in `packages/server/src/routes.ts` to `FlowStore.filePath()` in `packages/server/src/store.ts` without an identifier allow-list. The router applies `decodeURIComponent` to the id, and `path.join()` then normalizes traversal outside the configured flow directory after appending the .yaml extension. An attacker can read accessible YAML files as YAML-parsed JSON or permanently delete accessible .yaml files outside that directory, exposing configuration or secrets and disrupting dependent services. In `packages/server/src/index.ts`, CORS `origin: true` permits any browser origin, enabling a malicious webpage to target a loopback-bound instance. Docker deployments default to `HOST=0.0.0.0` and permit direct unauthenticated network access. This issue is fixed in repository release 0.3.7.

OpenHop es una herramienta para crear diagramas de flujo de datos interactivos. Versiones anteriores a la 0.3.7, “@openhop/server” pasa parámetros de ruta de flujo no autenticados de “GET /api/flows/:id” y “DELETE /api/flows/:id” en “packages/server/src/routes.ts” a “FlowStore.filePath()” en “packages/server/src/store.ts” sin una lista de permitidos de identificadores. El router aplica “decodeURIComponent” al ID, y “path.join()” luego normaliza el recorrido fuera del directorio de flujo configurado después de añadir la extensión .yaml. Un atacante puede leer archivos YAML accesibles como JSON parseado de YAML o eliminar permanentemente archivos .yaml accesibles fuera de ese directorio, exponiendo configuraciones o secretos e interrumpiendo servicios dependientes. En “packages/server/src/index.ts”, CORS “origin: true” permite cualquier origen de navegador, lo que permite a una página web maliciosa atacar una instancia vinculada a loopback. Las implementaciones de Docker por defecto usan “HOST=0.0.0.0” y permiten acceso de red directo no autenticado. Este problema se ha corregido en la versión 0.3.7 del repositorio.

USB Test is a lightweight Windows CLI utility for verifying sector integrity and detecting overreported capacity on USB flash drives. Prior to version 1.1.5, getSectorSize() in USB Test/src/driveinfo.cpp trusts DISK_GEOMETRY.BytesPerSector returned by IOCTL_DISK_GET_DRIVE_GEOMETRY without checking whether the call succeeded or enforcing size bounds. USB Test/src/drivetest.cpp uses the value for division and to size a heap buffer before memcpy(buffer.data(), &sector, 8), so a physically connected malicious USB storage device can report a value below eight bytes and cause repeated out-of-bounds writes, or report zero and cause a divide-by-zero denial of service when a user starts a drive test. The heap corruption can crash the elevated application and may permit arbitrary code execution. This issue is fixed in version 1.1.5.

USB Test es una utilidad ligera de línea de comandos (CLI) para Windows que verifica la integridad de los sectores y detecta la capacidad sobreinformada en unidades flash USB. Versiones anteriores a la versión 1.1.5, “getSectorSize()” en USB Test/src/driveinfo.cpp confía en “DISK_GEOMETRY.BytesPerSector” devuelto por “IOCTL_DISK_GET_DRIVE_GEOMETRY” sin verificar si la llamada tuvo éxito o sin aplicar límites de tamaño. USB Test/src/drivetest.cpp utiliza el valor para la división y para dimensionar un búfer en el heap antes de “memcpy(buffer.data(), &sector, 8)”, por lo que un dispositivo de almacenamiento USB malicioso conectado físicamente puede informar un valor inferior a ocho bytes y causar escrituras fuera de límites repetidas, o informar cero y causar una denegación de servicio por división por cero cuando un usuario inicia una prueba de unidad. La corrupción del heap puede bloquear la aplicación elevada y podría permitir la ejecución de código arbitrario. Este problema se corrige en la versión 1.1.5.

FOG is a free open-source cloning/imaging/rescue suite/inventory management system. Prior to 1.5.10.2253 and 1.6.0-RC-1, an authenticated API-enabled user with uType=1 who possesses both the user's API token and the global FOG API token can use PUT /fog/storagenode/{id}/edit to modify Storage Node user, pass, and ftppath fields because the API validates the credentials but does not enforce an administrator-only role. With storage replication enabled and a usable Storage Node, FOGImageReplicator interpolates those fields into an lftp command executed through proc_open() by the root-running service, allowing the low-privileged user to execute commands as root. This issue is fixed in versions 1.5.10.2253 and 1.6.0-RC-1.

FOG es un sistema de gestión de inventario/suite de clonación/creación de imágenes/rescate de código abierto y gratuito. Versiones anteriores a la 1.5.10.2253 y a la 1.6.0-RC-1, un usuario autenticado con API habilitada y uType=1 que posee tanto el token de API del usuario como el token de API global de FOG puede usar PUT /fog/storagenode/{id}/edit para modificar los campos de usuario, contraseña y ftppath de un nodo de almacenamiento (Storage Node) porque la API valida las credenciales pero no impone un rol exclusivo de administrador. Con la replicación de almacenamiento habilitada y un nodo de almacenamiento (Storage Node) utilizable, FOGImageReplicator interpola esos campos en un comando lftp ejecutado a través de proc_open() por el servicio que se ejecuta como root, lo que permite al usuario con pocos privilegios ejecutar comandos como root. Este problema está corregido en las versiones 1.5.10.2253 y 1.6.0-RC-1.

SimulationCraft is a tool to explore combat mechanics in World of Warcraft. In builds after release-820-01 and before the identified May 7, 2026 nightly, the `bcp_api.cpp` loop over the JSON `sockets` array uses `slot_data["sockets"].Size()` without bounding `gem_idx` by `MAX_GEM_SLOTS`, which is four in `engine/sc_enums.hpp`. The destination `gem_id` and `gem_bonus_id` arrays in `engine/item/item.hpp` have only four elements. More than four socket entries therefore write beyond `gem_id` into the adjacent `gem_bonus_id` vector storage; `bonus_list` entries can also access `gem_bonus_id` out of bounds. Corrupting a vector's `_M_start` pointer causes the `item_t` destructor to free an attacker-influenced pointer during normal cleanup. The advisory reports crashes and code execution demonstrated in a testing environment. Attack inputs can arrive through a malicious `.simc` profile with a `[[equipment]]` section, a compromised addon export, or `Battle.net API` responses modified by an attacker with a privileged network position. The fix is contained in the nightly build identified as simc-1205-01-516b5d7; no containing release tag is available.

SimulationCraft es una herramienta para explorar las mecánicas de combate en World of Warcraft. En las compilaciones posteriores a release-820-01 y anteriores a la versión nocturna identificada del 7 de mayo de 2026, el bucle de “bcp_api.cpp” sobre el array JSON “sockets” utiliza “slot_data[“sockets”].Size()” sin limitar “gem_idx” por “MAX_GEM_SLOTS”, que es cuatro en “engine/sc_enums.hpp”. Los arrays de destino “gem_id” y “gem_bonus_id” en “engine/item/item.hpp” tienen solo cuatro elementos. Por lo tanto, más de cuatro entradas de socket escriben más allá de “gem_id” en el almacenamiento del vector adyacente “gem_bonus_id”; las entradas de “bonus_list” también pueden acceder a “gem_bonus_id” fuera de los límites. Corromper el puntero “_M_start” de un vector hace que el destructor de “item_t” libere un puntero influenciado por el atacante durante la limpieza normal. El aviso informa de fallos y ejecución de código demostrados en un entorno de pruebas. Las entradas de ataque pueden llegar a través de un perfil “.simc” malicioso con una sección “[[equipment]]”, una exportación de complemento comprometida o respuestas de la “API de Battle.net” modificadas por un atacante con una posición de red privilegiada. La corrección está contenida en la compilación nocturna identificada como simc-1205-01-516b5d7; no hay una etiqueta de lanzamiento que la contenga disponible.

Xibo is an open source digital signage platform with a web content management system and Windows display player software. Prior to 4.4.3, missing object-level authorization on `/notification/export/{id}` allows an authenticated user to download attachments from any notification, including notifications created by administrators, by iterating over `sequential notification IDs`. Exploitation requires access to the `Notification Centre` to view past notifications, a privilege granted to non-administrators as standard. This issue is fixed in version 4.4.3.

Xibo es una plataforma de señalización digital de código abierto con un sistema de gestión de contenido web y software de reproductor de pantalla para Windows. Versiones anteriores a la 4.4.3, la falta de autorización a nivel de objeto en “/notification/export/{id}” permite a un usuario autenticado descargar archivos adjuntos de cualquier notificación, incluidas las creadas por administradores, al iterar sobre los ’ID de notificación secuenciales’. La explotación requiere acceso al ’Centro de Notificaciones’ para ver notificaciones anteriores, un privilegio concedido a los usuarios no administradores de forma estándar. Este problema se solucionó en la versión 4.4.3.

Xibo is an open source digital signage platform with a web content management system and Windows display player software. Prior to 4.4.3, missing access-control checks on `GET /layout/status/{id}` allow an authenticated user with any privileges to view the `status and metadata` of any layout, including layouts for which the user does not have view rights. This issue is fixed in version 4.4.3.

Xibo es una plataforma de señalización digital de código abierto con un sistema de gestión de contenido web y software de reproductor de pantalla para Windows. Versiones anteriores a la 4.4.3, la falta de comprobaciones de control de acceso en “GET /layout/status/{id}” permite a un usuario autenticado con cualquier privilegio ver el estado y los metadatos de cualquier diseño, incluidos los diseños para los que el usuario no tiene derechos de visualización. Este problema está solucionado en la versión 4.4.3.

Xibo is an open source digital signage platform with a web content management system and Windows display player software. Prior to 4.4.3, missing authorization on `POST /displaygroup/criteria/{displayGroupId}` allows an authenticated user to send criteria updates to any display via `XMR`. These criteria determine schedule changes and can alter playback, for example by causing content scheduled for rainy weather to play when it is not raining. Exploitation requires `Schedule Criteria` to be in use on the CMS. This issue is fixed in version 4.4.3.

Xibo es una plataforma de señalización digital de código abierto con un sistema de gestión de contenido web y software de reproductor de pantalla para Windows. Versiones anteriores a la 4.4.3, la falta de autorización en “POST /displaygroup/criteria/{displayGroupId}” permite a un usuario autenticado enviar actualizaciones de criterios a cualquier pantalla a través de “XMR”. Estos criterios determinan los cambios de programación y pueden alterar la reproducción, por ejemplo, haciendo que el contenido programado para clima lluvioso se reproduzca cuando no está lloviendo. La explotación requiere que los Criterios de Programación estén en uso en el CMS. Este problema está solucionado en la versión 4.4.3.

Shopper is a Headless e-commerce Admin Panel. From 2.8.0 until 2.8.1, three Shopper Livewire admin components retain authorization gaps after the earlier team-settings authorization fix. A staff member with only `view_users` and `access_dashboard` can mutate permissions, create an administrator, or delete roles. In `packages/admin/src/Livewire/Components/Settings/Team/Permissions.php`, `togglePermission` and `removePermission` authorize `view_users` rather than the stronger `access_setting` permission; `packages/admin/resources/views/livewire/components/settings/team/permissions.blade.php` exposes permission IDs in `wire:click` handlers. The attacker can grant arbitrary permissions to the bound role, including `access_setting` on the attacker's own role, or delete permission definitions. In `packages/admin/src/Livewire/SlideOvers/CreateTeamMember.php`, `mount()` and `store()` also accept `view_users`, and the client-selected `role_id` can identify the admin role, allowing creation of a pre-verified administrator with an attacker-chosen password. In `packages/admin/src/Livewire/Pages/Settings/Team/RolePermission.php`, `deleteAction` has no action authorization and is only conditioned on `can_be_removed`, while page access requires `view_users`. Deleting a removable role removes access for assigned users, enabling RBAC denial of service as well as privilege escalation. This issue is fixed in version 2.8.1.

Shopper es un Panel de Administración de comercio electrónico Headless. Desde la versión 2.8.0 hasta la 2.8.1 incluida, tres componentes de administración de Shopper Livewire conservan lagunas de autorización después de la corrección de autorización de configuración de equipo anterior. Un miembro del personal con solo ’view_users’ y ’access_dashboard’ puede modificar permisos, crear un administrador o eliminar roles. En ’packages/admin/src/Livewire/Components/Settings/Team/Permissions.php’, ’togglePermission’ y ’removePermission’ autorizan ’view_users’ en lugar del permiso más fuerte ’access_setting’; ’packages/admin/resources/views/livewire/components/settings/team/permissions.blade.php’ expone los ID de permiso en los manejadores ’wire:click’. El atacante puede otorgar permisos arbitrarios al rol vinculado, incluyendo ’access_setting’ en el propio rol del atacante, o eliminar definiciones de permisos. En ’packages/admin/src/Livewire/SlideOvers/CreateTeamMember.php’, ’mount()’ y ’store()’ también aceptan ’view_users’, y el ’role_id’ seleccionado por el cliente puede identificar el rol de administrador, permitiendo la creación de un administrador preverificado con una contraseña elegida por el atacante. En ’packages/admin/src/Livewire/Pages/Settings/Team/RolePermission.php’, ’deleteAction’ no tiene autorización de acción y solo está condicionado por ’can_be_removed’, mientras que el acceso a la página requiere ’view_users’. Eliminar un rol removible elimina el acceso para los usuarios asignados, lo que permite la denegación de servicio RBAC, así como la escalada de privilegios. Este problema se ha solucionado en la versión 2.8.1.

Ninja Forms plugin for WordPress before 3.15.4 contains an incomplete server-side validation vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to submit arbitrary values to Checkbox List, Multi-Select List, Image List, Country, and State fields because NF_Abstracts_List falls through to a validate() method that only checks required-field presence. Attackers can submit crafted formula payloads through the unauthenticated nf_ajax_submit endpoint that bypass CSV escaping applied only to Textbox and Textarea fields, resulting in CSV injection when an administrator downloads and opens the exported submissions file.

El plugin Ninja Forms para WordPress anterior a la versión 3.15.4 contiene una vulnerabilidad de validación incompleta del lado del servidor que permite a atacantes no autenticados enviar valores arbitrarios a los campos de Lista de Casillas de Verificación, Lista de Selección Múltiple, Lista de Imágenes, País y Estado porque NF_Abstracts_List pasa a un método validate() que solo verifica la presencia de campos obligatorios. Los atacantes pueden enviar cargas útiles de fórmulas manipuladas a través del endpoint no autenticado nf_ajax_submit que omiten el escape de CSV aplicado solo a los campos de Cuadro de Texto y Área de Texto, lo que resulta en inyección CSV cuando un administrador descarga y abre el archivo de envíos exportado.

russh is a Rust SSH client and server library that includes an SSH agent protocol implementation. From 0.50.0-beta.12 until 0.65.0, the agent server's Connection::try_sign path in russh/src/keys/agent/server.rs recognizes SSH_AGENT_CONSTRAIN_CONFIRM but returns a hard-coded successful result instead of calling Agent::confirm. In applications that override Agent::confirm to require user approval or another policy check, a process that can reach the agent socket, including the remote side of a forwarded agent, can use a key added through ssh-add -c without that check and can authenticate or sign data as the user while the key remains loaded. The separate Agent::confirm_request hook still runs for every signing request, so checks implemented there remain effective, and implementations that retain the default always-successful Agent::confirm do not lose an approval check through this regression. This issue is fixed in version 0.65.0.

russh es una biblioteca de cliente y servidor SSH de Rust que incluye una implementación del protocolo de agente SSH. Desde la versión 0.50.0-beta.12 hasta la 0.65.0, la ruta Connection::try_sign del servidor de agente en russh/src/keys/agent/server.rs reconoce SSH_AGENT_CONSTRAIN_CONFIRM pero devuelve un resultado exitoso codificado en lugar de llamar a Agent::confirm. En aplicaciones que anulan Agent::confirm para requerir la aprobación del usuario u otra verificación de política, un proceso que puede alcanzar el socket del agente, incluido el lado remoto de un agente reenviado, puede usar una clave añadida a través de ssh-add -c sin esa verificación y puede autenticar o firmar datos como el usuario mientras la clave permanece cargada. El hook separado Agent::confirm_request sigue ejecutándose para cada solicitud de firma, por lo que las verificaciones implementadas allí siguen siendo efectivas, y las implementaciones que mantienen el Agent::confirm predeterminado siempre exitoso no pierden una verificación de aprobación debido a esta regresión. Este problema está solucionado en la versión 0.65.0.

Echo is a Go web framework. From 4.0.0 until 4.16.1, Echo v4's opt-in BodyDump middleware reads complete request bodies into memory before handlers run and retains complete response bodies for the dump callback without capture limits. An unauthenticated client that can reach a route using BodyDump can submit large bodies or influence large responses, causing repeated or concurrent allocations that exhaust process memory. BodyDump is not enabled by default, and external request limits may reduce request-side exposure but do not bound response capture. This issue is fixed in 4.16.1.

Echo es un framework web de Go. Desde la versión 4.0.0 hasta la 4.16.1, el middleware BodyDump opcional de Echo v4 lee los cuerpos completos de las solicitudes en la memoria antes de que se ejecuten los manejadores y retiene los cuerpos completos de las respuestas para la devolución de llamada de volcado (dump callback) sin límites de captura. Un cliente no autenticado que pueda alcanzar una ruta que utilice BodyDump puede enviar cuerpos grandes o influir en respuestas grandes, causando asignaciones repetidas o concurrentes que agotan la memoria del proceso. BodyDump no está habilitado por defecto, y los límites de solicitudes externos pueden reducir la exposición del lado de la solicitud, pero no limitan la captura de respuestas. Este problema está corregido en la versión 4.16.1.

Echo is a Go web framework. From 4.0.0 until 4.16.1, Echo v4's opt-in Decompress middleware exposes a gzip-decoded request stream without limiting its expanded size. A small compressed request can expand into a very large body when a handler reads or binds it, consuming excessive memory or CPU and allowing repeated or concurrent requests to cause denial of service. The middleware is not enabled by default, and limiting only the compressed request size does not bound the decoded size. This issue is fixed in 4.16.1.

Echo es un framework web de Go. Desde la versión 4.0.0 hasta la 4.16.1 incluida, el middleware de descompresión opcional de Echo v4 expone un flujo de solicitud decodificado con gzip sin limitar su tamaño expandido. Una solicitud comprimida pequeña puede expandirse a un cuerpo muy grande cuando un manejador la lee o la vincula, consumiendo memoria o CPU excesivas y permitiendo que solicitudes repetidas o concurrentes causen denegación de servicio. El middleware no está habilitado por defecto, y limitar solo el tamaño de la solicitud comprimida no limita el tamaño decodificado. Este problema se corrige en la versión 4.16.1.

Echo is a Go web framework. From 4.15.0 until 4.16.1 and 5.4.1, Echo's Proxy middleware can retain a handler, copy goroutines, and network connections after a WebSocket client disconnects when the upstream keeps its connection open. The raw proxy waits for both copy directions without reliably closing the peer connection when one direction ends, including when a rejected upgrade response uses HTTP keep-alive. Repeated connections can accumulate resources and cause denial of service, depending on proxy-route accessibility, upstream behavior, and connection deadlines. This issue is fixed in 4.16.1 and 5.4.1.

Echo es un framework web de Go. Desde la versión 4.15.0 hasta las versiones anteriores a la 4.16.1 y a la 5.4.1, el middleware Proxy de Echo puede retener un manejador, copiar goroutines y conexiones de red después de que un cliente WebSocket se desconecte cuando el origen (upstream) mantiene su conexión abierta. El proxy sin procesar espera en ambas direcciones de copia sin cerrar de forma fiable la conexión del par cuando una dirección finaliza, incluso cuando una respuesta de actualización rechazada utiliza el keep-alive de HTTP. Las conexiones repetidas pueden acumular recursos y causar una denegación de servicio, dependiendo de la accesibilidad de la ruta del proxy, el comportamiento del origen (upstream) y los plazos de conexión. Este problema se ha corregido en las versiones 4.16.1 y 5.4.1.

Echo is a Go web framework. From 5.0.0 until 5.4.1, Echo v5's BodyDump middleware can discard a BodyLimit overflow error for an unknown-length request when BodyDump's capture limit is below the BodyLimit threshold. BodyDump drains the remaining body while ignoring read errors and replaces it with the captured prefix, so an HTTP/1.1 chunked request can be truncated and processed successfully even though the original body exceeded the configured limit. Known-length requests rejected before BodyDump runs are unaffected, and the issue does not establish a general authentication bypass or denial of service. This issue is fixed in 5.4.1.

Echo es un framework web de Go. Desde la versión 5.0.0 hasta la 5.4.1, el middleware BodyDump de Echo v5 puede descartar un error de desbordamiento de BodyLimit para una solicitud de longitud desconocida cuando el límite de captura de BodyDump está por debajo del umbral de BodyLimit. BodyDump vacía el cuerpo restante ignorando los errores de lectura y lo reemplaza con el prefijo capturado, por lo que una solicitud HTTP/1.1 fragmentada puede ser truncada y procesada con éxito a pesar de que el cuerpo original excedió el límite configurado. Las solicitudes de longitud conocida rechazadas antes de que se ejecute BodyDump no se ven afectadas, y el problema no establece una omisión de autenticación general ni una denegación de servicio. Este problema se ha solucionado en la versión 5.4.1.

Echo is a Go web framework. From 4.0.0 until 4.16.1 and 5.4.1, Echo's Proxy middleware selects a raw tunnel from a client WebSocket upgrade request before verifying that the configured upstream accepted the upgrade. If the upstream rejects the upgrade with an ordinary keep-alive response, later HTTP requests on the connection are sent directly to that upstream without passing through Echo's router or route-specific middleware. This can bypass authentication or authorization enforced only by Echo routes, but requires an accessible proxy route, a cooperating rejected-upgrade response, and a target without independent upstream authorization. This issue is fixed in 4.16.1 and 5.4.1.

Echo es un framework web de Go. Desde la versión 4.0.0 hasta la 4.16.1 y la 5.4.1, el middleware Proxy de Echo selecciona un túnel sin procesar de una solicitud de actualización de WebSocket del cliente antes de verificar que el upstream configurado aceptó la actualización. Si el upstream rechaza la actualización con una respuesta keep-alive ordinaria, las solicitudes HTTP posteriores en la conexión se envían directamente a ese upstream sin pasar por el router de Echo o el middleware específico de la ruta. Esto puede eludir la autenticación o autorización impuestas únicamente por las rutas de Echo, pero requiere una ruta de proxy accesible, una respuesta de actualización rechazada cooperativa y un objetivo sin autorización upstream independiente. Este problema se corrige en las versiones 4.16.1 y 5.4.1.

Echo is a Go web framework. From 5.0.0 until 5.4.1, Echo v5's ExtractIPFromRealIPHeader validates whether the client-supplied X-Real-IP value belongs to a trusted range instead of validating the direct network peer. A client reaching Echo directly, or through a proxy that preserves the header, can supply a loopback or private address and have Context.RealIP return that spoofed identity. Applications using the extractor for IP allowlists, rate limiting, audit logs, or forwarding headers can consequently trust an attacker-controlled address; the default direct extractor and Echo v4 are unaffected. This issue is fixed in 5.4.1.

Echo es un framework web de Go. Desde la versión 5.0.0 hasta la 5.4.1 incluida, la función ExtractIPFromRealIPHeader de Echo v5 valida si el valor X-Real-IP suministrado por el cliente pertenece a un rango de confianza en lugar de validar el par de red directo. Un cliente que accede a Echo directamente, o a través de un proxy que conserva la cabecera, puede proporcionar una dirección de bucle invertido o privada y hacer que Context.RealIP devuelva esa identidad suplantada. Las aplicaciones que utilizan el extractor para listas blancas de IP, limitación de velocidad, registros de auditoría o cabeceras de reenvío pueden, en consecuencia, confiar en una dirección controlada por el atacante; el extractor directo predeterminado y Echo v4 no se ven afectados. Este problema está solucionado en la versión 5.4.1.

n8n before 1.123.85, 2.43.5, and 2.44.1 contains an authorization bypass vulnerability that allows authenticated members to use inaccessible credentials through inline sub-workflow nodes with non-boolean disabled values. Attackers knowing a credential id can run Execute Workflow nodes in inline JSON mode that skip the permission check and send decrypted credentials to attacker-controlled servers.

n8n before 1.123.85, 2.43.5, and 2.44.1 contains a regular expression denial of service vulnerability that allows authenticated members to block the event loop via crafted glob patterns. Attackers who can create and run workflows can submit a wildcard-heavy File(s) Selector pattern causing exponential backtracking, making the UI, API, webhooks, and health checks unresponsive until restart.

n8n before 1.123.85, 2.43.5, and 2.44.1 contains a credential guard bypass vulnerability that allows editors of shared workflows to use restricted credentials by loading sub-workflows from URLs or local files. Attackers can configure the Execute Sub-workflow node with source url or localFile to serve content that resolves project credentials and returns their decrypted values.

n8n before 1.123.83, 2.41.4, and 2.42.1 contains a server-side request forgery vulnerability in the Slack Trigger webhook that allows unauthenticated attackers to exfiltrate Slack tokens by bypassing signature verification when no signing secret is set. Attackers who know the webhook URL can name a file to download, causing the node to send the workspace access token to an attacker host and return the response.

MONAI before 1.6.1 contains an insufficient integrity verification vulnerability in check_hash() that silently returns True when hash_val is None, with MD5 as the default hash type. Attackers performing man-in-the-middle or registry compromise can substitute bundles, datasets, or model archives downloaded without hashes, enabling malicious file delivery and potential code execution.

wasmtime-wasi in Wasmtime before 36.0.18, 37.0.0 before 48.0.6, and 49.0.0 before 49.0.3 re-appends a trailing slash to rename source paths, causing renameat on macOS and FreeBSD hosts to follow directory symlinks. A guest with sandbox write access can rename a relative symlink such as "up/" to move host directories into its sandbox and read or write them.

Due to the improper implementation of access control rules, malicious actors could perform a Server Side Request Forgery (SSRF) attack on affected WSO2 Products. Exploiting this vulnerability allows a malicious actor to access both internal and external resources, available through the network or filesystem. This could potentially lead to unauthorized access to sensitive data and systems, regardless of whether these resources are located within a private network, as long as they are reachable by the WSO2 product.

Debido a la implementación incorrecta de las reglas de control de acceso, el producto WSO2 acepta entradas suministradas por el usuario relacionadas con la ubicación del recurso sin aplicar las restricciones de validación esperadas. Un actor no autenticado puede explotar esto para dirigir al servidor a realizar solicitudes a ubicaciones de red arbitrarias.\n\nExplotar esta vulnerabilidad permite a un actor malicioso acceder a recursos internos y externos, disponibles a través de la red o del sistema de archivos, que son alcanzables por el producto WSO2. Esto podría conducir a un acceso no autorizado a datos y sistemas sensibles.

affectedData.product: WSO2 Identity Server as Key Manager

descriptions.value: An access control bypass flaw was identified in Samba's vfs_ceph_rgw module in it's openat() function. An authenticated user can bypass access controls to read or overwrite restricted files on shares configured with the experimental vfs_ceph_rgw module. When a client requests an existing file using mismatched character casing, the module fails to perform a case-insensitive lookup correctly, causing the server to treat the operation as creating a new file. As a result, the server skips standard permission checks on the existing file, allowing the attacker to access or overwrite sensitive data owned by other users.

A remote attacker may be able to terminate a process that passes attacker-controlled input to the P-384 VOPRF API without bounding its length. This vulnerability is addressed in swift-crypto version 5.0.3.

An attacker who controls the registry, a mirror, or the network path to it may be able to serve arbitrary image content in response to a pull by digest, so that a user runs an image other than the one they pinned. The fix compares the returned digest to the pinned digest and fails the pull on a mismatch. Tag pulls are exempt, because a tag is mutable by design. The fix also verifies the hash of manifests and blobs when they are fetched. This vulnerability is addressed in container version 1.6.0 and containerization version 0.52.1.
